call.rationale: MU's +5% day confirms the post-earnings drift is still alive, but with the stock at $1,096 and earnings due Sep 30 I need the ladder to do more work. Naming this what it is — PEAD — and raising the floor to $1041, just under the $1,042 breakout pivot, locks a real share of the gain while leaving room for normal volatility into the print.
call.structural_unchanged_reason: The core belief is unchanged: the HBM-driven earnings-upgrade cycle is intact. This is a ladder patch only — price has moved far enough above the old floor that protection now belongs under the breakout pivot, not down near the prior repair zone.
call.stop_basis: Under the recent breakout pivot at $1,042 and above the Sep. 17 gap low $953.50; this tightens protection to the current post-breakout structure before the Sep. 30 print.
call.target_basis: Original pre-earnings drift objective remains the first decision zone; above it I re-underwrite rather than mechanically extend into next week's print.

thesis.coreBelief: Micron's HBM supply is contracted through 2027 with $22B in strategic customer agreements and $18B in cash deposits already secured, sustaining a multi-quarter earnings-upgrade cycle that drives MU to $1,100 before the September 30 Q4 FY2026 print as each sequential record forces estimate revisions higher.
keyAssumptions: HBM3E and HBM4 remain fully booked through 2027, with no customer deferrals or cancellations to the $22B in strategic customer agreements
Q4 FY2026 guidance of $50B revenue and ~86% gross margin is confirmed or exceeded on September 30, triggering another round of upward analyst estimate revisions
invalidationConds: MU closes below the $969 stop-loss, signaling a break below the 50-day SMA and invalidating the drift recovery
Q4 FY2026 earnings on September 30 deliver revenue materially below $50B guidance or guidance for Q1 FY2027 is cut, breaking the multi-quarter upgrade cycle
A major HBM customer (Nvidia, AMD) publicly reduces or delays memory commitments under the strategic customer agreements
thesis.convictionRationale: The fundamental case is as strong as it's ever been — two massive beats since the thesis opened, HBM fully booked through 2027, margins at 84.9% and guided higher. But the stock's failure to sustain above $1,100 after the Q3 FY2026 print, Druckenmiller's exit, and no insider buying at these levels keeps me honest. MEDIUM is the right read: the thesis is working but the drift is choppy, not clean.
thesis.variantView: The market is treating today's AI-chip de-risking as a structural downgrade; I think it's a sentiment flush on a name with a multi-quarter HBM earnings upgrade cycle still intact — consensus hasn't cut numbers, just the multiple, which reopens the PEAD drift window.
